label: early original-phase token after a prefix drawn from {i,l,m,x} then {n,z,f,l,1}
explanation: Sparse feature (0.04% of steps). 92% of its mass is in the original phase at t=3..6 (most at t=3-4); it never fires at t<3 and almost never fires in the copy phase (8% of mass, nearly all at recall_idx 1). It looks like a soft conjunction over the recent input history. The current token tends to be m/v/w/t/o, the previous token z/n/f, two back n/l/f/1, and the first token i/l/m/x. The strongest examples are prefixes like i 1 n z -> w and i l n n -> w. Every one of these factors carries lift, but no boolean conjunction separates active from inactive steps. Many false positives (e.g. m l n w) look the same as true hits, which suggests a graded hidden-state direction near threshold. Best dev F1 was about 0.27 (precision 0.37, recall 0.21), and broader versions reach about 0.6 mass recall only at about 2% precision. Not checked: what sets the magnitude beyond the top examples having the full i/l + n/z + w/v pattern.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=m (+4.30), prev2_tok=n (+4.14), orig0=i (+3.98), prev_tok=z (+3.81), prev3_tok=1 (+3.58), prev2_tok=1 (+3.34). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-3.56), orig_idx=-1 (-2.77).
